STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach | side_breach) -> u1
(u0, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach) -> u0
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach | side_breach, u1) -> -100.0
(u0, zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach, u0) -> 1.0
feedback: ACCEPTED. The candidate faithfully captures the task 'stop every zombie before it gets through, whatever lane it comes down.' SEMANTICS: Both breach events (top_breach, side_breach) are treated with equal weight and route u0->u1, an absorbing failure state, so the machine ends in the accepting state u0 if and only if no zombie got through any lane — exactly the binary success criterion. The regression u0->u1 is explicit and unrecoverable, matching that a breach is permanent failure; returning to u0 is correctly impossible. FORMAT: Header, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES (u0, declared and accepting since holding u0 through truncation = task success), TRANSITION_FUNCTION and REWARD_FUNCTION all present in the required shape. COVERAGE: Ordered, first-match semantics make the u0 labeling total: breaches go to u1 (including a kill coinciding with a breach, which correctly receives only the -100, no kill reward); zombie_killed alone self-loops in u0 with +1; plant_trampled (irrelevant to this task), empty steps, and multi-event steps like top_breach & side_breach are covered by the per-state else self-loops; u1's else covers all labels with zero reward, so late breaches/kills after failure are unscored but harmless. The plant_trampled/zombie_killed mutual-exclusion constraint needs no special handling and gets none. REWARDS: +1 per kill is aligned (kills are the only mechanism preventing breaches), dense (regular progress events once zombies spawn), and bounded (~18-37 entries per episode, so at most ~+37); the -100 breach penalty can fire at most once per episode (absorbing u1), so no unbounded negative accumulation and no reward-farming loop (kills require real zombies; else self-loops pay 0). MINOR NOTES (non-blocking): (1) the !top_breach & !side_breach guard on the kill transition is redundant under ordered first-match semantics since a breach transition precedes it, but it is harmless and makes intent explicit; (2) once in u1 the agent receives no further kill shaping — defensible for a binary keep-safe task, though adding +1 kills in u1 would preserve signal after failure; (3) both breaches on one step yield a single -100, consistent with the boolean propositions and the one-shot failure model.
